label: def:benzene-molecular-braid
title: Benzene $C_6H_6$ as a molecular braid
html:
Definition. Benzene C_6H_6 is the molecular braid of six carbon atoms and six hydrogen atoms, assembled iteratively from pre-computed atomic braids.

Strand count

  • 6 carbon atoms: 6 \times 18 = 108 strands
  • 6 hydrogen atoms: 6 \times 2 = 12 strands
  • Total: N_{\mathrm{mol}} = 120 strands, living in H_{120}(q)

Bond structure

Each carbon has valence 4. In benzene:

  • 2 electrons shared with adjacent carbons (C--C bonds)
  • 1 electron shared with hydrogen (C--H bond)
  • 1 electron participates in \pi delocalization

This gives:

  • 6 C--C \sigma bonds (single, 1 shared pair each)
  • 6 C--H \sigma bonds (single, 1 shared pair each)
  • 6 \pi electrons delocalized around the ring

Iterative construction

  1. Build C_1--H_1 unit: \mathcal{A}_{C_1} + covalent bond with H_1, reduce to NF in H_{20}(q).
  2. Add C_2--H_2: embed, apply C_1--C_2 \sigma bond and C_2--H_2 bond, reduce in H_{40}(q).
  3. Continue for C_3--H_3 through C_5--H_5, reducing at each step.
  4. Close the ring: apply C_6--H_6 and C_6--C_1 \sigma bond to form the cyclic structure, reduce in H_{120}(q).
  5. Add \pi electrons: 6 electrons form a threading link T(2, 6) around the ring.

The threading link of step 5 emerges from the LP dual as the optimal configuration for the remaining 6 electrons, rather than being postulated.
